verdicts.differ: both apps have the rule but behave differently
verdicts.one-sided: only one app has the rule

rules.title: Where the country parameters live
Claim amount shown at the period mileage rate
rules.statement: The screen shows amount = miles x period rate BP-MRATE (GBP per mile, 3 decimals) ROUNDED to the penny; the amount is display-only and not stored on the claim.

rules.title: Prorated taxable benefit, truncated
rules.statement: Taxable benefit = (list price x benefit % / 1200 - monthly contribution) x car days / period days, truncated (not rounded) to the penny in GBP and floored at 0; the contribution is prorated with the benefit.

rules.title: Single country rule set DE
rules.statement: All parameters (minimum grade, benefit %, commute %, mileage rate) come from the one fleet_rule row with country 'DE': min_grade 6, benefit_pct 1.00, commute_pct 0.030, mileage_rate 0.305 EUR/km.

rules.difference: MF: mileage rate per BENEFIT-PERIOD (BP-MRATE) and benefit % per VEHICLE (VH-BPCT); DE: one fleet_rule row DE (min_grade, benefit_pct, commute_pct, mileage_rate) read by literal.

tests.name: GF01_countryParametersComeFromProfile
tests.proves: each country profile supplies its own parameter values; no country name in code

decision.decision: Country-wide values (grade threshold, mileage rate, DE 1% and 0.03%/km, rounding modes) live in each country's profile; per-vehicle benefit percent and per-employee contribution stay as vehicle and employee data.

rules.title: Company-car grade threshold
Company car grade threshold
rules.statement: An employee whose grade EM-GRD is below 07 is refused a company car on the assign screen ('GRADE NOT ELIGIBLE FOR A COMPANY CAR'); grades 07 and above are eligible.

rules.title: Assign screen re-entry skips grade and not-found checks
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, pressing ENTER on the assign screen re-reads the employee by id and proceeds to store the assignment without re-checking that the employee exists or that grade >= 07.

rules.title: Grade threshold for a company car
rules.statement: An employee is entitled to a company car only if grade (Entgeltgruppe) >= fleet_rule.min_grade (DE: 6); grades 1-5 are refused.

rules.difference: MF: EM-GRD >= 07, tested only in FLEASGN-PREMAP and bypassable by re-keying the id because FLEASGN-ENTER has no grade test; DE: grade >= fleet_rule.min_grade (6) tested in checkEmployee, and step 2/3 are only rendered after it passes. Same grade numbers are used for the 15 transferees on both sides although the thresholds differ (07 vs 6).

tests.name: GF02_gradeBelowThresholdIsRefused
tests.proves: profile threshold refuses lower grades on every step including confirm

tests.name: GF02_gradeAtThresholdIsEligible
tests.proves: profile threshold admits the threshold grade

tests.name: GF02_batchRunListsBelowThresholdHolders
tests.proves: monthly run taxes below-threshold holders as normal and lists them on the control report

decision.decision: Grade threshold from each country profile (UK 07, DE 6), checked on every step including confirm and in the monthly batch path; existing below-threshold holders keep their car until return, taxed as normal, listed on the migration report; the monthly run taxes them as normal and lists each on its control report as below grade threshold.

rules.title: Employee existence and status
Current employment record chosen over terminated ones
rules.statement: When an employee id has several occurrences (rehire), the online dialogs skip occurrences with status T (terminated) and use the next duplicate in storage order; transferred (X) occurrences are treated like active ones.

rules.title: Employee who has left
rules.statement: If every occurrence of the id is terminated (T), the inquiry and assign screens report 'EMPLOYEE HAS LEFT'; the mileage screen and the assign ENTER have no such exit.

rules.title: Employee must be on file
rules.statement: Inquiry, assign (premap) and mileage claim (enter) reject an unknown employee id with 'EMPLOYEE NOT ON FILE'.

rules.title: Employee id required
rules.statement: Inquiry ENTER with a blank employee id shows 'ENTER AN EMPLOYEE ID'; assign premap with blank id shows 'ENTER EMPLOYEE AND VEHICLE'.

rules.title: Requester must exist and be active
rules.statement: A car request is only accepted for an employee whose number (trimmed, upper-cased) exists and whose status is 'A'; any other status (e.g. 'T') is refused.

rules.title: Statement not restricted to active employees
rules.statement: The statement is computed for any employee number found (exact match, no trim/upper-case), including status 'T'.

rules.difference: MF: skips T duplicates in storage order, X (transferred) passes as current, ENTER paths have no not-found exit; DE: employee_no is unique, request requires status A, statement/assignment pages accept any status (no trim/upper-case).

tests.name: GF03_unknownEmployeeIsRejected
tests.proves: an unknown or blank employee number is rejected on every function

tests.name: GF03_employeeStatusGatesCarRequest
tests.proves: which employee statuses may request a car, as decided

decision.decision: Only active employees can request a car or file mileage, except a leaver may file claims dated on or before the leaving date; unknown numbers refused; statements/inquiry available for leavers and transferees.

rules.title: Rehire duplicates: one record per employment

crosscheck.topic: Rehire duplicates / one record per employment

rules.title: Each employment occurrence paid separately
rules.statement: Every EMPLOYEE occurrence is processed and written separately in database-key order, identified by employee id plus db-key, so a rehired person can get two output records in one period.

rules.title: Unique keys
rules.statement: Vehicle id and benefit period (YYYYMM) are unique; employee id may repeat (rehires) and duplicates are stored last.

rules.difference: MF keeps one EMPLOYEE occurrence per employment (CALC DUPLICATES LAST; 2 ids in the unload have a T and an A occurrence) and pays each occurrence separately keyed by db-key; DE employee_no is UNIQUE so a rehire reuses one row.

tests.name: GF04_rehireEmploymentsAreKeptApart
tests.proves: a rehire's earlier and current employments, assignments and claims stay distinguishable after migration

decision.decision: One person per employee number with an employment history (hire/leave dates); cars and claims attach to the employment they fall in; tax and leaver rules use that employment's dates.

rules.title: Cars per employee
No limit on cars per employee
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, assigning a car does not check whether the employee already holds a car or has an open assignment, so one employee can hold several cars at once.

rules.title: One open car per employee
rules.statement: An employee who already has an open assignment (end_date null) cannot request another car.

rules.difference: MF has no check (20 unload employees hold two open cars); DE refuses a request when an open assignment exists (0 seed employees with two open).

tests.name: GF05_secondOpenCarIsRefused
tests.proves: an employee with an open assignment cannot get another

tests.name: GF05_unconfirmedDoubleHoldersBlockCutover
tests.proves: the 20 UK NC+RP double holders stay on the fleet confirmation list until return dates are confirmed

decision.decision: One open car per employee in both countries. The 20 UK employees holding an open NC and RP are listed for fleet to confirm actual return dates before cutover; their affected-period tax waits on that.

rules.title: Vehicle selection for an assignment
Vehicle must exist to be assigned
rules.statement: Assigning a vehicle id that is not on file is rejected with 'VEHICLE NOT ON FILE'; vehicle ids are unique.

rules.title: Pool car availability
rules.statement: A pool car is offered only if it has no owner AND no open assignment; the list is sorted by plate and is computed once when step 1 passes.

rules.title: Pool choice requires a selected car
rules.statement: When 'pool' is chosen (the default), a vehicle must be selected before step 3.

rules.title: New car mandatory data
rules.statement: When registering a newly delivered car, plate, make, model, list price (EUR) and CO2 (g/km) are all mandatory; fuel defaults to Diesel 'D' (choices D/P/H/E). No range check on price or CO2.

rules.title: Plate normalisation on entry
rules.statement: A new car plate is trimmed, inner whitespace collapsed to one space and upper-cased; blank becomes missing.

rules.difference: MF keys an existing VH-VEHID (no vehicle maintenance in source); DE picks from the computed pool list or registers a new car (plate normalised, make/model/price/CO2 required) inside the request.

tests.name: GF06_assignmentRequiresKnownOrRegisteredVehicle
tests.proves: an assignment names an existing vehicle or registers a new one, as decided

decision.decision: Pick from the pool or register a new car; the profile decides the required fields (UK also benefit %); list price > 0, CO2 >= 0; no direct vehicle-id entry.

rules.title: One holder per car
A held vehicle cannot be assigned again
rules.statement: A vehicle currently linked to an employee as their held car (EMP-VEHICLE member) is refused with 'VEHICLE ALREADY HELD'.

rules.title: Pool loans are not 'held' cars
rules.statement: An assignment with reason PL (pool loan) is stored but the vehicle is not linked to the employee as their held car; reasons NC and RP (and anything else) link it.

rules.title: Pool car availability
rules.statement: A pool car is offered only if it has no owner AND no open assignment; the list is sorted by plate and is computed once when step 1 passes.

rules.title: No re-check at submit (pool race)
rules.statement: The pool car chosen in step 2 is not re-checked for availability at submit, so two concurrent wizards can assign the same pool car.

rules.title: Owner mirrors open assignment
rules.statement: A car's owner is set when an assignment opens and cleared when it is returned; owner is meant to equal the holder of the open assignment.

rules.difference: MF: "held" = EMP-VEHICLE member; PL pool loans never connect, so a car out on pool loan can be assigned again; DE: available = owner null AND no open assignment, checked at step 1 only (no re-check at submit, no DB constraint).

tests.name: GF07_staleSubmitIsRefusedCarNoLongerAvailable
tests.proves: a submit for a car taken since step 2 is refused and returns to vehicle choice

tests.name: GF07_poolLoanCountsAsHolding
tests.proves: a car on a PL pool loan cannot be assigned again

tests.name: GF07_oneOpenAssignmentPerCarConstraint
tests.proves: database refuses a second open assignment per vehicle

decision.decision: A car has at most one open assignment, pool loans included; re-checked at submit and enforced in the database; a late submitter gets car-no-longer-available and returns to vehicle choice with a fresh pool list.

rules.title: Assignment reason code
Assignment reason defaults to new car
rules.statement: If no reason is keyed the assignment reason defaults to NC (new car); values other than NC/RP/PL are accepted unchecked.

rules.difference: AS-RSN NC/RP/PL (default NC, unchecked) has no portal equivalent; portal records car_request status DELIVERED instead.

tests.name: GF08_assignmentReasonIsRecorded
tests.proves: assignment reason handling, as decided

decision.decision: Assignment reason from fixed list NC/RP/PL, default NC, other values refused; migrated DE assignments carry reason not recorded.

rules.title: Assignment start date
Assignment starts open on a keyed start date
rules.statement: A new assignment takes the keyed start date (8 numeric digits, required) and an end date of 0 meaning still open; the start date is not checked against hire date, leaving date, today or the vehicle's other assignments.

rules.title: Handover date default and no checks
rules.statement: The handover (start) date defaults to today, entered as dd.MM.yyyy, with no check against past/future or previous assignments.

rules.difference: Both accept any start date without plausibility checks; MF requires a keyed YYYYMMDD (digits only), DE defaults to today in dd.MM.yyyy.

tests.name: GF09_assignmentStartDateIsValidated
tests.proves: start date default and plausibility checks, as decided

decision.decision: Assignment start date required, defaults to today, must fall within the employee's employment, after the car's last return, and in an open period.

rules.title: Assignment identifier
Assignment identifier
rules.statement: Each new assignment id is 'A' followed by a 9-digit counter incremented by 1 per assignment.

rules.difference: MF AS-ASGID = A + session counter (never read); DE uses BIGSERIAL ids.

tests.name: GF10_assignmentIdentifierIsUnique
tests.proves: assignment id format and uniqueness, as decided

decision.decision: One global id scheme for new assignments; migrated UK rows keep their A+9-digit id as a legacy reference.

rules.title: Car request record delivered at once

crosscheck.topic: Car request record delivered at once

rules.title: Request is delivered immediately
rules.statement: Submitting the wizard in one transaction: stores a new car (registered_on = handover date) or reuses the pool car, sets the car's owner to the employee, records a car_request with status 'DELIVERED' and requested_on = today, and opens an assignment starting on the handover date with no end date.

rules.difference: DE writes car_request DELIVERED plus the assignment and vehicle owner in one transaction; MF stores only the ASSIGNMENT (and EMP-VEHICLE connect).

tests.name: GF11_carRequestIsRecorded
tests.proves: car-request record and status, as decided

decision.decision: Both countries record a car request with status delivered in the same transaction as the assignment; migration does not invent requests for existing UK assignments.

rules.title: Assignments and claims belong to an employee

crosscheck.topic: Mandatory ownership of assignments and claims

rules.title: Claims and assignments belong to an employee
rules.statement: Every assignment must belong to one employee and one vehicle, and every claim to one employee (mandatory automatic); a claim's period link is optional.

rules.difference: Portal has no rule id but the same constraint as NOT NULL FKs (assignment.employee_id/vehicle_id, mileage_claim.employee_id).

tests.name: GF12_assignmentAndClaimRequireOwner
tests.proves: an assignment without employee or vehicle, or a claim without employee, is rejected by the schema

rules.title: Current car shown to the user

crosscheck.topic: Current car shown to the user

rules.title: Inquiry shows latest car, even if returned
rules.statement: The inquiry screen shows the employee's assignment with the latest start date and its vehicle, without checking whether it has ended; if there is none it says 'NO COMPANY CAR HELD'.

rules.title: Current car is first open assignment
rules.statement: The employee's current car is the first assignment without end date in start-date-descending order; history shows all assignments incl. returned.

rules.difference: MF inquiry shows the latest-starting assignment even if returned; DE shows the first open assignment (start desc) and full history.

tests.name: GF13_currentCarIsOpenAssignment
tests.proves: which assignment is shown as the current car, as decided

decision.decision: The current car is the open assignment (only one allowed, GF05); none open shows no company car; history lists every car.

rules.title: Finding the assignment to return
Return only an open assignment
rules.statement: A car can only be returned if the vehicle's most recently stored assignment is still open (end date 0), else 'ALREADY RETURNED'; unknown vehicle gives 'VEHICLE NOT ON FILE' and a never-assigned one 'VEHICLE NEVER ASSIGNED'.

rules.title: Return lookup by exact plate
rules.statement: A return is found by exact, case-sensitive plate match (no normalisation) and must have an open assignment, otherwise an error is shown.

rules.difference: MF keys vehicle id and takes the last-stored VEH-ASSIGN member (ALREADY RETURNED if ended); DE looks up exact case-sensitive plate and any open assignment.

tests.name: GF14_returnFindsOpenAssignment
tests.proves: how a return finds its open assignment and the not-found messages, as decided

decision.decision: A return finds the car by plate (normalised as at registration, GF06) or vehicle id and closes its single open assignment; none open gives already returned.

rules.title: Return date not before start
Return date not before start
rules.statement: The return date (8 digits, required) must not be earlier than the assignment start date ('RETURN DATE BEFORE START'); it becomes the assignment end date, with no upper bound or period check.

rules.title: Return date not before handover
rules.statement: Return date (default today) must not be before the assignment start date; same-day return and future dates are allowed.

rules.difference: Both reject a return date before the start, allow same day and future; MF YYYYMMDD keyed, DE defaults to today.

tests.name: GF15_returnBeforeStartIsRejected
tests.proves: a return dated before the start is rejected; same day and future dates are accepted

rules.title: Return releases the car
Return releases the held car
rules.statement: On return the vehicle is unlinked from the employee as held car (if linked), making it assignable again.

rules.title: Booking a return
rules.statement: Booking a return sets assignment.end_date = return date, clears the car's owner (back to pool) and stores a car_return with return date, odometer km and condition note, in one transaction.

rules.title: Owner mirrors open assignment
rules.statement: A car's owner is set when an assignment opens and cleared when it is returned; owner is meant to equal the holder of the open assignment.

rules.difference: Both close the assignment and release the car (EMP-VEHICLE disconnect / owner null); DE also stores a car_return row.

tests.name: GF16_returnReleasesCar
tests.proves: returning closes the assignment on the return date and makes the car assignable again

rules.title: Odometer on return
Odometer on return is not recorded
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, the return screen asks for an odometer reading but it is never processed or stored.

rules.title: Odometer mandatory on return
rules.statement: A return requires an odometer reading (km); no range or plausibility check against earlier readings.

rules.difference: MF map captures WK-ODO but never processes it; DE requires and stores odometer_km.

tests.name: GF17_returnOdometerHandling
tests.proves: odometer capture on return, as decided

decision.decision: Odometer reading required on return, whole number in the profile unit, not below the car's last recorded reading; the first UK return of each car has no prior reading.

rules.title: Return function reachable
Return screen not reachable from the menu
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, the menu offers only 1 inquiry, 2 assign, 3 mileage and X exit; the return dialog FLERETN has no route, so no reachable online path ends an assignment.

rules.difference: MF FLERETN has no menu route; DE return page is in the top navigation.

tests.name: GF18_returnFunctionIsReachable
tests.proves: the return function is reachable from navigation, as decided

decision.decision: Return is an ordinary function in both countries, reachable from navigation.
open_items: Question for fleet operations: how are UK assignments ended today? 18 UK assignments have end dates though no menu route reaches FLERETN and no source we hold explains it.

rules.title: Mileage claim date window
Mileage claims need an open current period
rules.statement: A mileage claim can only be made against the benefit period of the current calendar month (YYYYMM of today) and only if that period exists with status O (open); otherwise 'NO OPEN CLAIM PERIOD'.

rules.title: Journey date within the open period
rules.statement: The journey date must lie inclusively between the period start BP-STRT and end BP-END, else 'JOURNEY DATE OUTSIDE OPEN PERIOD'.

rules.title: New claims start SUBMITTED
rules.statement: A new claim is stored with status 'SUBMITTED', claim date default today (no date check), purpose defaulting to empty text.

rules.difference: MF: journey date must be inside the open current period; DE: claim date defaults to today with no check (any past or future date).

tests.name: GF19_claimDateWithinOpenOrLookbackPeriod
tests.proves: future dates refused; closed months accepted only within the profile lookback (UK 3, DE 2) and paid in the current period

decision.decision: Journey date must not be in the future and must fall in the open period, or in an earlier closed month within the profile limit (UK 3 months back, DE 2 months back), paid in the current period.

rules.title: Mileage distance required
Miles must be positive whole miles
rules.statement: Miles claimed are whole miles 1-99999 (5 digits, required); zero gives 'MILES REQUIRED'.

rules.title: Mileage claim km must be positive
rules.statement: A claim is accepted only with km > 0 (integer kilometres); no upper limit; preview (Berechnen) computes for any km including <= 0.

rules.difference: Both require a positive whole number; MF miles 1-99999 (map PIC 9(5)), DE km > 0 with no upper bound.
rules.note: Crosscheck pair says same; catalog says differ: mainframe caps at 99999 miles (5-digit field), portal has no upper limit.

tests.name: GF20_distanceWithinProfileMaximum
tests.proves: whole units 1..profile maximum (UK 1500 miles, DE 2500 km)

decision.decision: Whole units from 1 to the profile maximum: UK 1,500 miles, DE 2,500 km.

rules.title: Mileage amount and rate
Claim amount shown at the period mileage rate
rules.statement: The screen shows amount = miles x period rate BP-MRATE (GBP per mile, 3 decimals) ROUNDED to the penny; the amount is display-only and not stored on the claim.

rules.title: Mileage reimbursement from approved claims
rules.statement: Mileage reimbursed = sum over the employee's APPROVED claims dated within the period (inclusive) of miles x period rate, each claim ROUNDED to the penny before summing; total miles is the sum of those claims' miles. Pending and rejected claims are not paid.

rules.title: Mileage amount
rules.statement: Business-trip reimbursement = km x fleet_rule.mileage_rate (DE 0.305 EUR/km), rounded to 2 decimals HALF_EVEN (banker's rounding); the amount is frozen on the claim at submission.

rules.title: Statement mileage counts approved only
rules.statement: Reimbursed business-trip total = sum of amounts of claims dated in the month with status 'APPROVED'; SUBMITTED and REJECTED are excluded.

rules.difference: MF: amount not stored; batch recomputes miles x BP-MRATE (0.445 GBP/mile in all 13 periods) ROUNDED per claim at run time. DE: amount frozen at submit = km x 0.305 EUR/km HALF_EVEN, statement sums stored amounts.

tests.name: GF21_mileageRoundsHalfUpInBothCountries
tests.proves: per-claim amount rounds half-up to the cent in both profiles

tests.name: GF21_mileageAmountFrozenAtSubmission
tests.proves: a later rate change does not alter a submitted claim

tests.name: GF21_mileageReimbursementMatchesHoldouts
tests.proves: UK reimbursement reproduces the 12 holdout BENOUT files

decision.decision: Mileage amount = distance x profile rate, rounded half-up to the cent per claim in both countries, frozen at submission; only approved claims are paid. Expected change: 172 DE seed claims move by one cent versus legacy half-even.

expected_changes.change: amount moves by 0.01 EUR (half-even to half-up)

rules.title: Claim status and approval
New claims are pending approval
rules.statement: Every submitted claim is stored with status P (pending), id 'C' + 9-digit counter, linked to the employee and to the current benefit period, and the user sees 'CLAIM SUBMITTED FOR APPROVAL'.

rules.title: Mileage reimbursement from approved claims
rules.statement: Mileage reimbursed = sum over the employee's APPROVED claims dated within the period (inclusive) of miles x period rate, each claim ROUNDED to the penny before summing; total miles is the sum of those claims' miles. Pending and rejected claims are not paid.

rules.title: New claims start SUBMITTED
rules.statement: A new claim is stored with status 'SUBMITTED', claim date default today (no date check), purpose defaulting to empty text.

rules.title: Statement mileage counts approved only
rules.statement: Reimbursed business-trip total = sum of amounts of claims dated in the month with status 'APPROVED'; SUBMITTED and REJECTED are excluded.

rules.difference: Both store new claims as pending (P / SUBMITTED) and pay only approved (A / APPROVED); neither source has an approval step. Codes differ: A/P/R vs APPROVED/SUBMITTED/REJECTED.
rules.note: Neither source contains an approval step: the mainframe unload has A/R claims and the portal seed has APPROVED/REJECTED claims, but no code writes those statuses. Who approves claims is outside both sources.

tests.name: GF22_newClaimIsPendingAndOnlyApprovedIsPaid
tests.proves: a new claim is stored pending; only approved claims are paid

rules.title: Vehicle recorded on a claim
Claim records the employee's latest car
rules.statement: The claim records the vehicle of the employee's latest-starting assignment (even if returned) or spaces if they never had one; holding a company car is not required to claim mileage.

rules.difference: MF stores MC-VEHID of the latest assignment (643 of 1511 unload claims have one); DE mileage_claim has no vehicle column.

tests.name: GF23_claimVehicleHandling
tests.proves: whether a claim records a vehicle, as decided

decision.decision: A claim records the company car held on the journey date, or none.

rules.title: Claim history list
Claim history window
rules.statement: The mileage page lists the employee's claims with claim_date between now minus 6 months and now, oldest first, all statuses.

rules.difference: DE lists the last 6 months of claims; MF has no claim inquiry.

tests.name: GF24_claimHistoryWindow
tests.proves: claim history listing, as decided

decision.decision: Both countries list an employee's claims back over a profile-set window (6 months for both), newest first, all statuses.

rules.title: Mileage claim by a leaver or inactive employee

crosscheck.topic: Mileage claim by a leaver / inactive employee

rules.title: Employee who has left
rules.statement: If every occurrence of the id is terminated (T), the inquiry and assign screens report 'EMPLOYEE HAS LEFT'; the mileage screen and the assign ENTER have no such exit.

rules.title: Mileage claim accepted for any found employee
rules.statement: Mileage find/submit require only a found employee and positive kilometres. Status, leave date, grade and car ownership are not checked; leavers can submit claims too.

rules.difference: Shared: neither side applies an active-status or leave-date eligibility rejection before accepting a mileage claim. Portal find/submit accepts any found employee with positive kilometres; FleetService adds no status or leave-date guard. Mainframe-only: FLEMILE-PREMAP and FLEMILE-ENTER inspect EM-STAT and repeatedly OBTAIN DUPLICATE EMPLOYEE while it is T, rather than rejecting a leaver. ENTER checks not-found only before that loop; neither loop has an explicit not-found/end-of-duplicates exit. An all-T employee id therefore has a no-exit loop risk if the exhausted lookup leaves EM-STAT at T, not a guaranteed accepted claim. Once the loop finishes, ENTER checks journey date and miles, but not EM-LEAV or active status, before storing the claim.

tests.name: GF25_mileageClaimEligibility
tests.proves: status and leave-date checks on mileage claims, as decided

decision.decision: Linked to GF03 B: only active employees may file mileage, except a leaver may file claims dated on or before the leaving date.

rules.title: Benefit period lifecycle
Mileage claims need an open current period
rules.statement: A mileage claim can only be made against the benefit period of the current calendar month (YYYYMM of today) and only if that period exists with status O (open); otherwise 'NO OPEN CLAIM PERIOD'.

rules.title: Benefit run is for one period named on the parm card
rules.statement: The monthly run processes the single period YYYYMM from SYSIN cols 1-6; if that period is not on file the run aborts with RC 16.

rules.title: Run does not require a closed period
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, the benefit run does not check that the period is closed (BP-STAT C) and does not mark it run (BP-RUNDT).

rules.title: Statement default period
rules.statement: The benefit statement period is given as yyyy-MM; if empty it defaults to the previous calendar month (server clock); it covers day 1 to the last day of that month.

rules.title: No closed periods
rules.statement: Statements are computed on every view and never stored; there is no period open/close, so later changes (list price, commute km, returns) recompute past months.

rules.difference: MF has BENEFIT-PERIOD records with O/C status (claims only into the open current period; run takes a parm period, status not checked); DE has no period entity and recomputes any month on every view.

tests.name: GF26_benefitPeriodLifecycle
tests.proves: period open/close and recomputation, as decided

decision.decision: Both countries have monthly periods open -> closed; closing runs the benefit calculation and stores results; closed months are never recomputed.

rules.title: Benefit formula
Inquiry monthly benefit (full month)
rules.statement: The inquiry screen shows a monthly benefit = list price x benefit % / 1200 (annual % spread over 12 months) minus the employee's monthly contribution, ROUNDED to the penny (GBP) and floored at 0; it is never prorated for days.

rules.title: Prorated taxable benefit, truncated
rules.statement: Taxable benefit = (list price x benefit % / 1200 - monthly contribution) x car days / period days, truncated (not rounded) to the penny in GBP and floored at 0; the contribution is prorated with the benefit.

rules.title: Monthly benefit formula (1% + 0.03%/km)
rules.statement: Monthly benefit = list price x benefit_pct/100 + list price x commute_pct/100 x commute_km (DE: 1% + 0.03% per one-way commute km), unrounded.

rules.title: Benefit proration and rounding
rules.statement: Line benefit = monthly benefit x days / days in month, rounded to 2 decimals HALF_UP; total benefit = sum of rounded lines (EUR).

rules.difference: MF: list x VH-BPCT (per-vehicle annual %) / 1200 - EM-CNTRB, GBP; inquiry ROUNDED full month, batch prorated by car days and TRUNCATED, floored at 0. DE: list x 1% + list x 0.03% x commute_km per month, EUR, prorated by days/monthDays HALF_UP per line, no contribution, no floor, current list price and commute_km.

tests.name: GF27_benefitFormulaPerProfile
tests.proves: one formula; profile sets % source, commute component, contribution and benefit rounding

tests.name: GF27_benefitMatchesHoldouts
tests.proves: UK benefit reproduces holdout BENOUT for employee-months not affected by GF05/GF29

tests.name: GF27_benefitMatchesPortalStatements
tests.proves: DE benefit reproduces recorded statements

tests.name: GF27_inquiryShowsRunFigure
tests.proves: inquiry shows the prorated figure the run will tax

decision.decision: One benefit formula; each country profile sets benefit-% source, commute component, contribution deduction with floor at 0, and benefit rounding mode (UK truncate, DE half-up). The UK inquiry screen shows the same prorated figure the run will tax.

expected_changes.change: none from the formula itself (UK keeps truncation)
shows the prorated run figure instead of the full-month rounded figure

rules.title: Benefit days and period length
Days in period
rules.statement: Period length in days = BP-END - BP-STRT + 1 (inclusive calendar days).

rules.title: Car days in period
rules.statement: Car days = (earliest of period end, assignment end if set, leaving date if set) - (later of assignment start and period start) + 1 inclusive, or 0 if negative.

rules.title: Statement default period
rules.statement: The benefit statement period is given as yyyy-MM; if empty it defaults to the previous calendar month (server clock); it covers day 1 to the last day of that month.

rules.title: Benefit days per assignment
rules.statement: For each assignment overlapping the month, benefit days = inclusive days from max(start, 1st) to min(end or month-end, month-end); assignments not overlapping are skipped. Both the return day and a same-day new start count.

rules.difference: MF period dates come from the BENEFIT-PERIOD record (BP-STRT..BP-END); car days capped by AS-END and EM-LEAV. DE period = calendar month of yyyy-MM (default previous month), days capped by end_date only.

tests.name: GF28_swapDayCountsForIncomingCarOnly
tests.proves: calendar-month inclusive days; on a swap day only the incoming car counts

decision.decision: Calendar month, inclusive days; on a swap day only the incoming car counts, so nobody is taxed on two cars for the same day.

expected_changes.change: no assignment ends on the day the next one starts

rules.title: Which assignments are taxed in a period

crosscheck.topic: Which assignments are taxed in a period

rules.title: Only one car taxed per period
rules.statement: The taxed car is the employee's assignment with the latest start date that started on or before the period end; any other assignment overlapping the period is ignored.

rules.title: Selected car must overlap the period
rules.statement: The selected assignment yields benefit only if it is open (end 0) or ended on or after the period start; otherwise days = 0 and no car is reported.

rules.title: Pool loans and ineligible grades are taxed
rules.statement: As OBSERVED, the benefit run taxes the selected assignment regardless of its reason (including PL pool loans) and regardless of employee grade or status.

rules.title: Benefit days per assignment
rules.statement: For each assignment overlapping the month, benefit days = inclusive days from max(start, 1st) to min(end or month-end, month-end); assignments not overlapping are skipped. Both the return day and a same-day new start count.

rules.difference: MF taxes only the latest-starting assignment that started on or before period end (any reason incl. PL, any grade/status); DE sums a line for every assignment overlapping the month.

tests.name: GF29_everyHeldCarIsTaxed
tests.proves: every car held in the period is taxed

decision.decision: Tax every car the employee held in the period, in both countries; the never-closed UK legacy assignments must be resolved in migration first (see GF05).

expected_changes.scope: UK holdout employee-months with more than one overlapping assignment
expected_changes.change: additional cars taxed; 194 are stale NC+RP pairs (20 employees, resolved by GF05 fleet confirmation) and 4 genuine mid-month swaps; unresolved upper bound +115308.73 GBP taxable
portal already taxes every overlapping car

rules.title: Leavers: benefit cap and flag
Who is in the benefit run
rules.statement: An employee occurrence is considered if hired on or before the period end and either has no leaving date (0) or left on or after the period start; status, grade and cost centre are not tested.

rules.title: Car days in period
rules.statement: Car days = (earliest of period end, assignment end if set, leaving date if set) - (later of assignment start and period start) + 1 inclusive, or 0 if negative.

rules.title: Leaver flag
rules.statement: The output is flagged L when the leaving date falls within the period (start <= EM-LEAV <= end), otherwise blank.

rules.title: Statement days not capped at leaving date
rules.statement: Statement benefit days are the overlap of the assignment (start, end or month-end) with the calendar month only; employee.leave_date and hire_date are never read, so a leaver's open or late-closed assignment is taxed to the end of the month, and there is no leaver flag on the statement.

rules.difference: MF skips occurrences not employed in the period, caps car days at EM-LEAV and flags L; DE never reads hire_date/leave_date and has no leaver flag.

tests.name: GF30_leaverBenefitCapAndFlag
tests.proves: leaving-date cap and leaver flag, as decided

decision.decision: Both countries cap car days at the leaving date, exclude employees who left before the period, and flag leavers in the period with L.

expected_changes.change: no DE leaver holds a car past the leaving date

rules.title: Benefit output, control totals and payroll hand-off

crosscheck.topic: Benefit output, control totals and payroll hand-off

rules.title: No car reported when no car days
rules.statement: If car days are 0 the output carries a blank vehicle id and zero taxable benefit.

rules.title: Who gets an output record
rules.statement: An output record is written only when the employee has car days > 0 or approved miles > 0 in the period.

rules.title: Control totals
rules.statement: The control report ends with the number of records written, total taxable benefit and total mileage reimbursed, accumulated from the written records.

rules.title: Any database error aborts the whole run
rules.statement: Any unexpected IDMS status aborts the run with return code 16 and rollback, so the later count (STEP020) and payroll FTP (STEP030) steps are skipped by their COND=(4,LT).

rules.title: One output dataset per period
rules.statement: Each run creates a new catalogued dataset FLT.PROD.BENOUT.P<period>, so a second run of the same period fails allocation unless the dataset is deleted first.

rules.difference: MF writes BENOUT per period (new dataset, abort RC16 skips count and FTP); DE renders the statement only and persists nothing.

tests.name: GF31_periodCloseWritesOutputAndControlTotals
tests.proves: close writes one record per employee with car days or approved miles and control totals

tests.name: GF31_failedRunChangesNothing
tests.proves: a failed run rolls back

tests.name: GF31_closedPeriodCannotBeRerun
tests.proves: a closed month cannot be run again

decision.decision: On period close both countries write one output record per employee with car days or approved miles plus control totals (count, total taxable benefit, total mileage); a failed run changes nothing; a closed month cannot be re-run. UK sends the payroll file; DE has no payroll file for now.
open_items: German payroll has not agreed a payroll file format; DE payroll file to be added once agreed.

rules.title: Navigation shell
Menu options
rules.statement: Menu option 1 opens inquiry, 2 assign, 3 mileage claim, X/PF3/CLEAR leave; any other value shows 'INVALID OPTION'; PF3 on any function returns to the menu.

rules.title: Wizard back skips validation
rules.statement: 'Zurueck' goes back one step (not below 1) without validating input.

rules.difference: MF menu options 1/2/3/X and PF3 back to menu; DE top-nav links on every page plus a 3-step wizard with Zurueck.

tests.name: GF32_navigationReachesEveryFunction
tests.proves: navigation and back behaviour, as decided

decision.decision: Navigation reaches every function (inquiry, car request, mileage, statement, return, search) in both countries; Back saves the draft without validation and checks re-run on the next forward step.

rules.title: Employee search
Employee search
rules.statement: Search is a case-insensitive contains match on employee number, last name or first name, sorted by last then first name, at most 50 rows, showing each one's current car plate; empty term lists the first 50.

rules.difference: DE searches number/name contains, max 50; MF only exact id lookup.

tests.name: GF33_employeeSearch
tests.proves: employee search, as decided

decision.decision: Both countries get employee search: case-insensitive contains on employee number, last or first name, at most 50 rows sorted by last then first name, showing the current car.

rules.title: Refreshing the car-request wizard halfway through

mainframe.note: FLEASGN is a single screen; no multi-step request exists.

rules.title: Observed refresh behaviour (local probe)
rules.statement: F5 resends the POST and re-renders the same step; a plain GET restarts at step 1 with a new ViewState and loses entries; a repeated final submit creates no duplicate and lands silently on step 1; a stale step-3 submit after another session took the same pool car succeeds, leaving two open assignments and overwriting the owner; a graceful Tomcat restart keeps the session. Not tested: crash restart, 30-minute timeout.

rules.difference: Portal wizard state is view-scoped; mainframe has no wizard.

tests.name: GF34_refreshReturnsToSavedDraft
tests.proves: refresh and reload return to the same step with the entries

tests.name: GF34_newTabResumesSameDraft
tests.proves: a new tab for the same employee opens the same draft

tests.name: GF34_draftClearedOnSubmit
tests.proves: submit clears the draft

tests.name: GF34_draftCanBeDiscarded
tests.proves: discard removes the draft

tests.name: GF34_doubleSubmitCreatesOneRequest
tests.proves: a repeated final submit creates one request and shows it

tests.name: GF34_resumeRechecksEligibilityAndCar
tests.proves: resuming a draft re-checks eligibility and car availability; a draft does not reserve a car

decision.decision: A half-finished car request is saved as a server-side draft against the employee (one draft per employee, intentionally shared); refresh, reload or a new tab return to the same step with the entries; the draft does not reserve a car; resuming re-checks eligibility and car availability; final submit counts once; the draft lives until submitted (then cleared) or discarded via a discard action.
